title: Diagnostic Accuracy of In‐House Tests Against White Spot Syndrome Virus in Farmed Penaeid Prawns: A Scoping Review
content:
ABSTRACT

Managing white spot syndrome virus (WSSV) in prawn farms relies on fit-for-purpose in-house tests (IHTs), for instance, to confirm WSSV infection during disease outbreaks. Selecting and interpreting fit-for-purpose IHTs requires robust evidence on their diagnostic accuracy. We aimed to (i) conduct a scoping review to chart the WSSV IHTs evaluated for diagnostic accuracy and agreement in farmed penaeid prawns as of July 2026, and (ii) critically appraise, adapting the Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies 2 (QUADAS-2) guidance, the validity of diagnostic test evaluations (DTEs) that included at least one test meeting our eligibility criteria to be an ‘acceptable’ reference standard (RS). Systematically searching Scopus, Web of Science and PubMed platforms, with citation chasing, yielded 3031 unique records. After screening, we found 39 articles reporting DTEs of 87 distinct IHTs, yet 13 articles did not provide diagnostic accuracy estimates. Eight individual DTEs, each including at least one acceptable RS, were critically appraised. One DTE was deemed at high risk of spectrum bias while the remaining were at possible risk of review bias, mainly due to blinding usage and the test running order not being reported. Overall, the collective evidence of the diagnostic accuracy for any evaluated WSSV IHT was deemed shallow because of incomplete/flawed design, reporting approximation/omission or lack of replications. Recommendations to strengthen future DTE design and reporting are provided to enhance the validity and depth of the current collective evidence and support informed decisions when developing fit-for-purpose WSSV detection protocols for on-farm disease management.
